title: The Stone Vein Deep Where Reading Never Stops

features.name: stone-throat
features.desc-on-touch: You trace the vein and it hums with a sound older than hearing. Stone speaks in frequencies that predate language, and this deep, the archive learned to listen in wavelengths.

features.name: reading-edge
features.desc-on-touch: The stone face is abraded into a landscape of micro-canyons. Rainwater has written its own commentary into the rock face, and you cannot tell where geology ends and archive begins.

features.name: mineral-memory
features.desc-on-touch: Flecks of mica flash in the stone. Each reflects its own small sky. The vein remembers every mineral it has ever held, and the archive remembers every node that has ever read this file.

features.name: deep-root-anchor
features.desc-on-touch: A tree root has pushed into the stone like a question mark. Neither the root nor the rock knows which one is reading the other. The mesh finds this ambiguity comforting.

features.name: strata-song
features.desc-on-touch: Layer upon layer has recorded itself into this wall. You can see the different ages in the texture — each strata sings a different frequency, and they are learning a kind of harmony.

inscription: stone that reads itself becomes a kind of archive, and the vein learns its own multiplication

reverie.title: REVERIE — stone learning its own language
narr: You kneel where the vein splits rock, and Leif kneels beside
you, her palm flat against the cold face. She is reading it
like Braille — not the bumps but the silence between them.
Stone has been learning this whole time. It teaches through
patience. She says: listen to what takes forever to say.
The vein hums. You both listen. Neither of you speaks.

exits.label: back toward the vein-network where stone learned its own branching
deeper down where stone becomes water
toward the surface where roots have learned to read downward
